findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so report data and the seeded vendor roster spreadsheet are stored without enforced server-side encryption (no SSE-KMS, no customer-managed key control).
No ACL is specified and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so there is no guardrail preventing a public ACL or bucket policy from exposing report data.
No logging block is configured, so reads and writes to this data bucket leave no access record, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorised access.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so objects can be overwritten or destroyed with no recoverable prior version, weakening integrity protection for archived reports.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial export data unencrypted at rest with no key management control.
No logging block is configured, so access to sensitive financial exports is not auditable.
Versioning is absent while force_destroy = true, so ledger export objects can be silently overwritten or permanently deleted by anyone with write access, with no recoverable prior version.
The private ACL is the only control; no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block enforces it, so a later ACL or policy change could expose ledger data publicly.
The model artifacts bucket enables versioning and logging but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so proprietary model data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving the private ACL as the only barrier against accidental public exposure of model artifacts.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set, so operational runbooks, which commonly contain infrastructure detail, endpoints and occasionally credentials, are stored unencrypted at rest.
Server access logging is not configured, so access to runbook content is not recorded for audit or intrusion detection.
The bucket relies solely on a private ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block enforcement, leaving it exposed to later misconfiguration.

The ACL is the invalid value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" rather than "log-delivery-write", so the intended permission model for the log-delivery target bucket is not applied, risking failed log delivery or an unexpected access configuration on the bucket holding audit evidence.

force_destroy = true on the central audit/log-delivery bucket allows the entire audit trail, including logs from model_artifacts, to be deleted along with the bucket, undermining log integrity and non-repudiation.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards the audit log bucket, and its ACL is a (malformed) log-delivery grant rather than private, so an ACL or policy change could expose security logs publicly.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely third-party contact data/PII) is uploaded into the reports_archive bucket, which has no default encryption, and the object itself specifies neither server_side_encryption nor kms_key_id, so it is stored in cleartext at rest.
